title: Finite contractible-base diagrams and strict henselianity at maximal-coordinate primes
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative w-contractible ring [sk-def-pe-wlocal], let $D$ be a nonempty small directed poset, and let $(B_d,\varphi_{de})_{d\leq e}$ be a direct system of commutative $A$-algebras with unital $A$-algebra transition maps. Assume each $B_d$ is generated by a finite list as an $A$-module and is finitely presented as an $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $B=\varinjlim_d B_d$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with coprojections $\iota_d$. Then:
(1) Every $B_d$ is w-contractible, hence w-local and with strictly henselian localizations at maximal ideals [sk-def-pe-wlocal].
(2) Each structural map $A\to B_d$ and each transition map $\varphi_{de}:B_d\to B_e$ is module-finite and integral (every element of its target satisfies a monic polynomial over the image of its source), and contraction along any of these maps sends maximal ideals to maximal ideals.
(3) For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset B$ such that all $\mathfrak p_d=\iota_d^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$ are maximal in $B_d$, the fraction maps
$$(B_d)_{\mathfrak p_d}\longrightarrow (B_e)_{\mathfrak p_e},\qquad b/s\longmapsto\varphi_{de}(b)/\varphi_{de}(s)$$
are local homomorphisms, meaning that the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. The canonical fraction maps exhibit
$$B_{\mathfrak p}\cong\varinjlim_d(B_d)_{\mathfrak p_d}$$
as a colimit in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The ring $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and the contraction of $\mathfrak p$ under $A\to B$ is maximal in $A$.
Zero algebras and noninjective transition maps are allowed; clause (3) is conditional on the stated maximality of every contraction and does not assert that all primes or all maximal ideals of $B$ have that property.

source.place: Tag 0986, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-over-w-contractible; Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral; Tag 00OI, lemma-going-up-maximal-on-top with Tag 00GU, lemma-integral-going-up; Tag 037D, lemma-colimit-normal-ring, localization identity in proof; Tag 04GI, lemma-colimit-henselian, strict case. Inherited proof steps 1, 2, 7, 8.

proof.text: Apply [lem-ce-finite-finitely-presented-wcontractible] to $A\to B_d$: its hypotheses are exactly the assumed module-finiteness, algebra finite presentation and w-contractibility of $A$. Thus $B_d$ is w-contractible. By [sk-def-pe-wlocal], it is w-local and $(B_d)_{\mathfrak m}$ is strictly henselian for every maximal $\mathfrak m$. This proves (1). For independently quantified ring universes, lift both rings to their maximum universe, apply the existing same-universe theorem, and transport the result back along the ring equivalences. Both transports use the existing proved private theorem RingHom.wContractible_of_ringEquiv from WeilConjectures.RingTheory.WContractibleGeometricCriterion, accessed with a proof-only import all. It transports precisely the three fields of the w-contractible definition; no duplicate transport theorem is declared.

For $d\leq e$, choose finite $A$-module generators $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ of $B_e$. An expression $y=\sum_j a_jy_j$ is also $y=\sum_j\varphi_{de}(a_j\cdot1)y_j$, since the transition is an $A$-algebra map. Hence the same list generates $B_e$ as a $B_d$-module. Structural maps are module-finite by assumption, so all maps in (2) are module-finite.

source.place: Tag 00F3, definition-finite-type, finite ring maps; scalar restriction through the given A-algebra maps

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to every structural and transition map from step 2. They are integral, including with nonzero kernels. Then [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal] shows that each contracts every maximal ideal of its target to a maximal ideal of its source. This proves (2).

source.place: Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral; Tag 00OI, lemma-going-up-maximal-on-top, using Tag 00GU, lemma-integral-going-up

proof.text: Fix the prime $\mathfrak p$ in (3) and put $\mathfrak p_d=\iota_d^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$. The cocone equations imply $\varphi_{de}^{-1}(\mathfrak p_e)=\mathfrak p_d$. Construct the diagram using the canonical localization maps [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; their identities and composition follow by localization homomorphism extensionality. The same construction on the coprojections gives a cocone with apex $B_{\mathfrak p}$. To prove its colimit property, restrict any cocone to the original rings and use the given colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] to obtain a map out of $B$. Every denominator outside $\mathfrak p$ comes from a stage by [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], where it is already a unit. The map therefore extends uniquely to $B_{\mathfrak p}$. Localization homomorphism extensionality and the original colimit homomorphism extensionality verify factorization and uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 037D, lemma-colimit-normal-ring, first paragraph of proof; localization universal property and representative existence in filtered ring colimits

proof.text: Each map in the constructed localization diagram is Localization.localRingHom for the contraction equality from step 4. Mathlib Localization.isLocalHom_localRingHom proves it local, and IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_comap gives the required equality of maximal-ideal inverse images. Thus the elementary fraction calculation of this step is supplied by the existing localization API [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization; Tag 07BH, local rings, prime localization paragraph

proof.text: Each $\mathfrak p_d$ is maximal by the hypothesis of (3), so step 1 makes each localized stage strictly henselian. Steps 4 and 5 verify all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-filtered-colimit-strictly-henselian-local]; applied to that colimit cocone it makes $B_{\mathfrak p}$ strictly henselian. Choose $d\in D$. The contraction of $\mathfrak p$ to $A$ equals the contraction of $\mathfrak p_d$ along $A\to B_d$, which is maximal by step 3. This finishes (3).

CommAlgCat.{u} A) (hfinite : ∀ d : D, Module.Finite A (F.obj d)) (hfp : ∀ d : D, Algebra.FinitePresentation A (F.obj d)) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit ((forget₂ (CommAlgCat.{u} A) CommRingCat.{u}).mapCocone c)) : (∀ d : D, IsWContractibleRing (F.obj d)) ∧ (∀ d : D, (algebraMap A (F.obj d)).Finite ∧ (algebraMap A (F.obj d)).IsIntegral ∧ ∀ (m : Ideal (F.obj d)), m.IsMaximal → (m.comap (algebraMap A (F.obj d))).IsMaximal) ∧ (∀ (i j : D) (hij : i ≤ j), (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom.toRingHom.Finite ∧ (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom.toRingHom.IsIntegral ∧ ∀ (m : Ideal (F.obj j)), m.IsMaximal → (m.comap (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom.toRingHom).IsMaximal) ∧ (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum c.pt, (∀ d : D, (p.asIdeal.comap (c.ι.app d).hom.toRingHom).IsMaximal) → IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) ∧ (p.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A c.pt)).IsMaximal ∧ ∃ (L : D ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (hL : ∀ d : D, L.obj d = CommRingCat.of (Localization.AtPrime (p.asIdeal.comap (c.ι.app d).hom.toRingHom))), (∀ (i j : D) (hij : i ≤ j), CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (F.obj i) (Localization.AtPrime (p.asIdeal.comap (c.ι.app i).hom.toRingHom))) ≫ eqToHom (hL i).symm ≫ L.map (homOfLE hij) = CommRingCat.ofHom (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom.toRingHom ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (F.obj j) (Localization.AtPrime (p.asIdeal.comap (c.ι.app j).hom.toRingHom))) ≫ eqToHom (hL j).symm) ∧ (∀ (i j : D) (hij : i ≤ j), (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (p.asIdeal.comap (c.ι.app j).hom.toRingHom))).comap (eqToHom (hL i).symm ≫ L.map (homOfLE hij) ≫ eqToHom (hL j)).hom = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (p.asIdeal.comap (c.ι.app i).hom.toRingHom))) ∧ ∃ (l : Cocone L) (hl : l.pt = CommRingCat.of (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)), (∀ d : D,
